title: Pool-burst measurement of sacrifice replacement capacity, and eager respawn (rejected)
impact: Experiment B of the peer-recommended estimand split after exp 241's confounded send-vs-sacrifice A/B: measure the **pool-replacement-capacity** question cleanly. Uses the pool's decode-free observable — dispatch queue-wait (`workerAssignedAt - requestEnqueuedAt`), via a benchmark-only `ReaderPool.debugDispatchTimings` collector (null in production). Decisive test: a production **4-worker** pool, **8** identical large (sacrificing) selects behind a barrier (1-4 grab workers, 5-8 park), measure the parked four's queue-wait, reset the pool between bursts (fresh-lifecycle treatment unit, unlike exp 241's mutating pool). 40 bursts x 3 reps. A CONFIRMED code asymmetry motivated an **eager-respawn** candidate: the sacrifice reply handler completes the caller (a `Completer.sync()` running the whole dispatch/emit/flush chain) BEFORE initiating the replacement spawn, opposite of the sibling non-sacrifice branch. **Two reproducible findings, both counter to hypothesis:** (1) the **send** (no-sacrifice) lane has the HIGHEST parked queue-wait — highest in all 3 reps, ~+500 us / +19% over the sacrifice lanes — because a large result's SendPort graph copy blocks the worker longer than Isolate.exit + an overlapped respawn; so at pool-4 sacrifice is neutral-to-FAVORABLE, not a capacity drain. (2) sacrifice-eager (2684 us) equals sacrifice-current (2652 us) within ~1% (< any margin) on queue-wait and makespan — eager respawn buys nothing, because at pool-4 the respawn overlaps other workers' in-flight queries and is off the parked request's critical path. **Rejected: eager respawn.** Falsifies the suspected pool-capacity penalty at the production pool size and turns exp 241's hand-wavy 'keep sacrifice' into a measured result for the pool regime. Caveat: pool-4 overlap dilutes the raw per-sacrifice respawn gap and `Database.open` clamps readerCount>=2, so the pool-1 diagnostic ceiling isn't reachable via the public API. Kept the reusable queue-wait instrument + `RESQLITE_SACRIFICE_THRESHOLD` knob; the eager prototype is reverted. Still open from the split: Experiment A (intrinsic prepared-result handoff) and the text/shared-leaf misroute guard.
